objective: Establish the correct live-granularity expectation for the running bots. The 5m-close backtest was never a valid live comparator (live runners evaluate exits on 60s instantaneous spot prices; Alpha 1 enters LONG unconditionally - no momentum signal - and Alpha 2 uses momentum K=10 on 60s polls = 10-min momentum).
engine: runner-mirror on 1m closes: flat -> enter (churn: always long; momentum: sign of close[t]/close[t-K]-1), exit at first 1m close crossing +/-barrier from entry, timeout at bar 75, re-enter next bar; 3% of capital, 0.1%/side fees, circuit breaker 3 losses -> 50-bar cooldown (live semantics)

protocol.selection: rank by median combined net return over folds 1-3 (BTC+ETH shared capital)

gates.G2_persistence: positive net return on >= 2 of 3 train folds
gates.G4_fee_hurdle: validation fold mean per-trade net return > 0.002 (0.2% round-trip margin)

caveat: 1m CLOSES still understate live responsiveness (60s polls catch intra-minute crossings the 1m close straddles). If 1m says NO-GO while live keeps winning, residual gap = intra-minute capture or live regime artifact; the 50-trade live milestone decides.
comparison: live Alpha 1 4/4 and Alpha 2 3/3 wins vs this distribution's expected WR/net EV
